case_name: Gaya Yadav and others v State of Bihar and others
facts: The prosecution story, briefly stated is that ferd-beyan (Ext.2) was lodged by Lallan Bharti (PW3) that on 15.3.1987 at about 7.30 p.m. the deceased Jagannath Singh, who was the Mukhiya of Mau Gram panchayat, was meeting people in Mau Bazar...

The informant went back 4 to 6 steps from where he saw that Rahish Yadav and Khalitra Yadav were catching hold the two arms of the deceased and the accused Gaya Yadav and Bhagwat Yadav each fired a shot from the pistol at the deceased who fell down.
This witness, further, stated that Mukhiyajee was a nice man of the area and the witness supported him in every election.
issues: The legal questions or points of law being debated
petitioner_arguments: Undisputedly, this witness is an independent witness. Similarly, being close to the deceased the witness in the ordinary circumstances would not depose falsely against the accused and allow the real assailants being escaped unpunished.
respondent_arguments: Mr. Anoop G. Choudhary, learned senior counsel, strenuously urged that PW-3 deposed that Gaya Yadav and Bhagwat Yadav fired at him by a country made pistol upon which the victim fell down, whereas PW-10 Dr. Mithlesh Kumar Sinha found only one gun shot injury.
court_reasoning: The testimony of PW-3 has been assailed by counsel for the appellants on the ground that his ocular testimony is in contradiction with the medical evidence.
holding: By a common judgment the High Court has dismissed their appeals and confirmed the conviction as recorded by the Trial Court.
cases_cited: Gaya Yadav and others v State of Bihar
